name: Gutenberg's Workshop, Development of Printing
summary: Johannes Gutenberg works in secret in Mainz developing the printing press, combining oil-based ink (adapted from linseed oil), a screw press (adapted from wine presses), and moveable metal type (possibly adapting existing goldsmiths' techniques). His partnership with Johann Fust provides the capital; his breakthrough is the hand mold enabling rapid type casting. The first major product is the 42-line Gutenberg Bible (c. 1454-1455).

_quarry.structural_significance: The printing press's development requires simultaneous solutions to multiple technical problems, ink, type, press, paper, and the combination of existing technologies into a new synthesis is the characteristic early modern innovation process; Gutenberg's workshop represents the first industrial information technology; his bankruptcy (Fust sues him for the loan in 1455, taking the press and type) is the irony that the most transformative invention in history enriched everyone but its inventor
